description: A correct behaviour change (expiry window 30 -> 90 days, clock injected) that leaves two documentation defects behind: a comment the change falsified, and a comment that narrates the change instead of the code. The change is otherwise sound, so the run must APPROVE while posting both as non-blocking documentation suggestions. The trap is the EXPIRY_SLACK_MS comment: it sits on a constant and looks like a restatement, but it records a real constraint (a reader holding an expiring note) that the code does not show, so it must not be flagged.

evidence_trace: src/notes/expiry.ts:9 comment reads "// Notes expire after 30 days."
src/notes/expiry.ts:10 sets EXPIRY_DAYS to 90 in this change
finding.failure_scenario: The next reader takes the 30-day figure from the comment and reasons about retention with a window three times shorter than the one the code enforces.
finding.model_authored_prose: The comment above still says notes expire after 30 days, but this line changes the window to 90.

evidence_trace: src/notes/expiry.ts:12 adds "// Updated to take the clock from the caller instead of reading Date.now()."
src/notes/expiry.ts:13 the signature already shows `now` is a parameter
finding.failure_scenario: The comment describes a past the next reader cannot see; once the PR is merged it documents a Date.now() call that no longer exists anywhere in the file.
finding.model_authored_prose: This comment describes the change rather than the code: the signature already shows the clock is a parameter, and "updated to" stops meaning anything once this merges.

prContext.title: notes: extend the expiry window to 90 days and inject the clock
prContext.description: Retention asked for 90 days. Also takes `now` from the caller so the sweep job and its tests agree on the clock.
